record.title: Nscale S-1 reports 461,000 active and contracted GPUs and $103.4B in active and contracted TCV
record.summary: Nscale's September 18, 2026 SEC registration statement reports that as of August 31 it had approximately 25,000 active GPUs and 461,000 active and contracted GPUs, with $2.6 billion of active and $103.4 billion of active and contracted total contract value (TCV) under long-term take-or-pay customer contracts. The filing defines TCV as revenue contracted over the committed term of signed agreements, excluding optional extensions, renewals and unexercised capacity. These figures provide an issuer-reported denominator for contracted AI infrastructure scale, but they do not establish that contracted GPUs are installed or delivered, or that the stated contract value will be recognized as revenue or collected.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Nscale's SEC filing reports approximately 25,000 active GPUs and 461,000 active and contracted GPUs as of August 31, 2026; active-and-contracted is not synonymous with installed or delivered capacity.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The filing reports $2.6 billion active and $103.4 billion active and contracted TCV under long-term take-or-pay contracts as of August 31, 2026. The issuer defines TCV as contracted revenue over signed agreements' committed terms and excludes optional extensions, renewals and unexercised capacity; the figure is not recognized revenue or cash collected.

evidence_gaps.description: The aggregate filing does not provide a contract-by-contract reconciliation from contracted GPUs and TCV to installed capacity, customer acceptance and recognized revenue.
No independent audit of contracted GPU delivery, active capacity, utilization or contract-level performance was examined in this activation.

brief.importance_rationale: If the issuer-reported contracts are delivered, the scale materially affects assessments of AI compute supply, infrastructure financing and delivery risk. The filing reports large contracted commitments but not full installed capacity or realized revenue, so the consequence is substantial while economic realization remains unverified.
limitations: The figures are issuer-reported in an SEC registration statement and were not independently audited by this review.
461,000 active and contracted GPUs do not mean 461,000 GPUs were installed, delivered, powered or utilized as of August 31, 2026; the filing separately reports approximately 25,000 active GPUs.
$103.4 billion active and contracted TCV is the issuer-defined contract value across committed terms, not recognized revenue, collected cash, profit or a measure of realized compute output.

Contract execution depends on financing, site construction, power availability, deployment schedules, customer acceptance, concentration and performance; this review did not reconcile those risks against each contract.
brief.summary: Nscale's September 18, 2026 SEC registration statement reports that as of August 31 it had approximately 25,000 active GPUs and 461,000 active and contracted GPUs, with $2.6 billion of active and $103.4 billion of active and contracted total contract value (TCV) under long-term take-or-pay customer contracts. The filing defines TCV as revenue contracted over the committed term of signed agreements, excluding optional extensions, renewals and unexercised capacity. These figures provide an issuer-reported denominator for contracted AI infrastructure scale, but they do not establish that contracted GPUs are installed or delivered, or that the stated contract value will be recognized as revenue or collected.

technical.claimed_result: Nscale reports that its long-term take-or-pay contracts represent $103.4B of active-and-contracted TCV and support approximately 461,000 active-or-contracted GPUs as of August 31, 2026.
technical.compute_or_cost: Not measured in this review. Aggregate GPU counts and TCV do not disclose utilization, delivered GPU-hours, power draw, capital cost per GPU or realized margin.
technical.demonstrated_result: The SEC filing itself documents what Nscale reported, including approximately 25,000 active and 461,000 active-and-contracted GPUs and $2.6B active plus $103.4B active-and-contracted TCV as of August 31, 2026. These are issuer-reported contract and infrastructure metrics, not independently audited delivery outcomes.
technical.implementation_status: The filing reports a mixture of active and contracted GPUs and sites. This activation did not reconcile individual sites, delivery milestones, customer acceptance or recognized revenue to the aggregate metrics.
technical.mechanism: Long-term customer contracts, including take-or-pay arrangements, support Nscale's planned and active GPU infrastructure deployment. The filing aggregates active and contracted capacity and TCV; the reported categories include facilities and GPUs at different deployment stages.
technical.novelty: The filing provides a large, dated primary-source denominator for contracted AI infrastructure and distinguishes active capacity and TCV from broader active-and-contracted commitments.
technical.regime: Issuer-reported infrastructure and signed customer contracts in Nscale's September 18, 2026 SEC registration statement; data as of August 31, 2026. TCV covers signed agreements' committed terms and excludes optional extensions, renewals and unexercised capacity.
technical.reproducibility: The SEC filing is publicly accessible and its issuer-reported definitions and figures can be checked directly. Contract-by-contract delivery and revenue outcomes were not independently reproduced or audited.
technical.strongest_baseline: The filing compares active and active-and-contracted TCV of $2.6B and $103.4B as of August 31, 2026, with $0.5B active and $38.0B active-and-contracted TCV as of December 31, 2025. The filing also reports approximately 25,000 active GPUs against 461,000 active and contracted GPUs.

brief.title: Nscale S-1 reports 461,000 active and contracted GPUs and $103.4B in active and contracted TCV
brief.why_it_matters: A $103.4B active-and-contracted TCV base and 461,000 active-or-contracted GPU count, if delivered as described, would represent a very large infrastructure commitment and make deployment, financing, customer concentration and contract execution central to the AI compute supply outlook. The filing gives a concrete issuer-reported denominator, while the active-versus-contracted split and the long committed terms require careful separation from live capacity, recognized revenue and realized economics.
